narrative.text: Archbishop Renek arrives at the Palace at 2:00 AM, unannounced. He looks like he hasn't slept in days. He asks to speak with you in the private chapel. He falls to his knees.

Chancellor, I am being eaten alive by guilt. In 1942, the Church provided the BNI with a list of 'subversive' priests. We handed them over to be executed. I signed that list. I have carried this sin for 20 years. I need to know what to do.

The Archbishop is confessing to aiding Halvek's purges. He handed priests to the executioners. If he makes this public, the Church's authority collapses, but civil liberties are vindicated. If I bury it, I protect the Church but damn my own soul. If I use it as blackmail, I become Halvek.

choices.text: Tell him to confess publicly. The truth must be known.
Bury it forever. The Church must remain stable.
Use it as blackmail. The Church now does what you say.

narrative.text: He confessed publicly three days later, at the Sunday service. The chapel was full. The statement was two minutes long and contained no excuses. The congregation sat in silence when he finished. By Monday morning, two diocese leaders had requested transfers. By Wednesday, the reformists were citing it in Assembly speeches about accountability. Renek did not resign. He said penance was not done by walking away. I don't know if that is wisdom or cowardice. He is still Archbishop.
Attendance at Ashenmere Cathedral falls by a third over the next two months, then recovers to within nine percent. The nine percent write letters. Renek answers every one by hand.

choices.text: Renek confessed from the pulpit. The cathedral lost a third of its people and won most of them back.

narrative.text: I told him the Church needed to remain stable. He thanked me. He meant it. He went home and slept for the first time in weeks, I imagine. The list stays where it has always been — in the archive, misfiled, accessible to anyone who knows where to look. I have protected an institution. The men on that list remain unacknowledged. The Church keeps its authority. I keep the knowledge of what that authority cost.
There are fourteen names on the misfiled list. Three of the men are still alive. One of them is a parish priest in Thornfeld who baptized two children last Sunday.

choices.text: The list stays misfiled. Fourteen names, three of them living, one still baptizing.

narrative.text: I told him what I needed. He understood immediately — the posture of a man who has spent his life in institutions where leverage is the primary currency. The Church votes with my coalition on the housing bill. The education amendment. The civil liberties provision. Renek delivers every time, quietly, through back channels, with no public trace. He is useful. We both know what that means. He kneels at the altar every morning and I imagine he prays for something I cannot give him.
I will deliver your votes, Chancellor. Do not ask me to bless them.

choices.text: The Church votes with my coalition every time. Renek prays for something I can't give him.
